units.translation: Of things that happen uselessly and sharply. For ἐρείκη [heather] is a wild plant, which when it becomes dry is easily kindled. Similarly Sophocles fr. 746 said γραίας ἀκάνθης [of an old thorn-bush]. Grammarians disagreed about the spelling, some approving ἐρείκη, others ἐρίκη. ἐρίκη (with long ι) pleased Herodian: see Thes. vol. 3 p. 1093 and Lentz. Herodian. vol. 1 p. 317. Herodian gives the reason for his opinion vol. 2 p. 511, 1: ἐρίκη εἶδος φυτοῦ. ὤφειλε διὰ τῆς ει διφθόγγου γράφεσθαι, ἀπὸ γὰρ τοῦ ἐρείκω γέγονεν. ἀλλ᾽ ἔστι καινὼν ὁ λέγων ὅτι τὰ διὰ τοῦ ικη ἀποστρέφεται τὴν ει δίφθογγον [heather is a kind of plant. It ought to be written with the diphthong ει, for it comes from ἐρείκω. But there is a new rule saying that words in ικη avoid the diphthong ει]. Moreover, there is the same doubt about cognate names, such as Ἐρεικούσσα or Ἐρικοῦσσα, and others, on which see Thes. p. 1994.
having kindled a heap of old heather with fire.

and she tore her folded robe with the edge of her hands.
for the Thracian blasts tore the ships against each other.
Of the present εἴρῳ, I say, I speak, which the epic poets use, but the Attic writers did not use; the future is ἐρέω, contracted to ἐρῶ.

The aorist is εἶπον, of which another form also exists, declined after the first aorist, εἶπα (as the Alexandrians said ἔβαλα and ἦλθα). Of this the second person εἶπας, εἴπατε and the imperative εἰπάτω, εἴπατε the Attic writers preferred to use rather than εἶπες, εἴπετε, εἰπέτω, εἴπετε: on which see what is said in the Thesaurus vol. 3 p. 1946. Therefore the first person in Aeschylus is consistently εἶπον, the second εἶπας, the plural εἶπον. The imperative is εἰπέ, the optative εἴποιμι, the subjunctive εἴπω, the infinitive εἰπεῖν. The participle is εἰπών, εἰπόντος, εἰπόντι, εἰπόντα. The examples are these, arranged according to the order of the plays.
